column3: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in the fictional gene SYNTHKIN1 reduce functional checkpoint protein, so the synthetic mitotic checkpoint complex cannot restrain anaphase onset. Cells divide before chromosomes are correctly attached, producing missegregation and mosaic aneuploidy, which is proposed to impair progenitor expansion and yield growth restriction and microcephaly.
column7: Aneuploidy in this synthetic model is established during early development. Post-natal restoration of checkpoint signalling would not reverse structural findings already present at birth; a mechanistically correct agent can still be therapeutically irrelevant. Any benefit would be limited to slowing ongoing missegregation and its sequelae.
